statements.text: You have previously learned the central tendency (mean - domain - mode) and used them to calculate a set of data to identify one value describing the trend of these data in centeralization around this value.
The mean = (total of these values) / (their number). Formula: $\text{The mean}=\dfrac{\text{Total of these values}}{\text{Their number}}$
Dispersion of any set of values means divergence, or the differences between its values.
The dispersion is small if the differences between the values are little, whereas the dispersion is great if the differences between the values are very big.
When the dispersion is zero, all the values are equal.
The dispersion is a measure that expresses how homogeneous the sets are.
To compare two or more sets of data, we must have a measure of central tendency and another measure of dispersion for each set.
The range is the difference between the greatest value and the smallest value in the set.
(1) The range is the simplest and easiest method of measuring dispersion.

(2) The range is influenced greatly by the outlier. The values of the second set disperse in a range of 50; when the last value (92) is removed the range = 52 - 42 = 10, or 1/5 of the previous range. Formula: $52-42=10=\frac{1}{5}\times 50$
(3) The range is not influenced by any value in the set except the greatest and smallest values, so it does not give a clear picture of the dispersion of the set.

Standard deviation is the commonest measure of dispersion and the most accurate (under certain conditions); it is the positive square root of the average of the squared deviations of the values from the mean.
Standard deviation σ equals the square root of (the sum of (x − x̄)² divided by n). Formula: $\sigma=\sqrt{\dfrac{\sum (x-\bar{x})^2}{n}}$
σ (sigma) denotes the standard deviation of the society (population) of data.
x̄ (x Bar) denotes the mean of the values of the society.
n denotes the number of values.
∑ denotes addition (summation).
The standard deviation is affected by the deviations of all the values and its value is affected by the outlier.
For any frequency distribution, the standard deviation σ equals the square root of Σ(x - x̄)²k divided by Σk. Formula: $\sigma=\sqrt{\dfrac{\sum (x-\bar{x})^2 k}{\sum k}}$
x represents the value or the center of the set.
k represents the frequency of the value or the set.
Σk is the total of frequency. Formula: $\sum k$
x̄ is the mean, equal to Σxk divided by Σk. Formula: $\bar{x}=\dfrac{\sum xk}{\sum k}$
First: Set the calculator to the statistical system to enter data (keys On, Mode, 2 (Stat), then 1 (1-VAR); screen shows X and FREQ columns).
Second: Calculate the standard deviation of the frequency distribution (Example 2).
Step 1: Enter the centers of sets 2, 6, 10, 14, 18 (keys: On, Mode, 2, 1, then 2 = 6 = 10 = 14 = 18 =).
Step 2: Go to the top of the second column (FREQ) and enter the corresponding frequency for each set 2, 5, 8, 15, 10.
Step 3: Recall sum (standard deviation) (keys Shift 1 5 (VAR) 3 (X σn) =); then $\sigma \simeq 4.521$.
Step 4: Go back to the original system and switch off the calculator.

The standard deviation has the same measuring units as the original data, so it is used to compare the dispersion of sets which have the same measuring units when the mean is equal. The set which contains more standard deviation is more dispersed.
